subject: Dedicated capacity: Horizon Labs traffic annotation & session probe
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@horizonlabs.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — traffic annotation & session probe

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Horizon is very interested in a Dedicated deployment for our internal annotation and model-assist workflows. Before we get on a sizing call, the engineering team asked whether you can share the types of telemetry you need to create an initial capacity estimate.

Top-level asks from our side:
- We run a mix of interactive annotation sessions (chat-like) and bulk batch inference jobs for labeling.
- Peak day concurrency: ~420 concurrent annotators during our morning surge (09:00–11:00 PT).
- Average prompt length (chat): 45 tokens; average model response length: 220 tokens.
- Batch jobs: 1.2M short requests/day (prompt ~15 tokens, response ~30 tokens) run overnight; throughput-oriented.
- We operate a few long-running sessions that maintain KV caches per session for multi-turn context (session TTL ~6 hours).

I've attached a small sample of the prompt mix and a clip of our session logs to help. Happy to surface more telemetry if helpful. Can you confirm what fields you need (token histogram, p99 latency target, percent of streaming responses, etc.) so we can prepare?

Regards,
Priya Shah
Head of Infrastructure
Horizon Labs

[Attachment: horizon_prompt_sample.csv (csv, 48KB)]
[Attachment: session_log_sample.json (json, 1.1MB)]

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya@horizonlabs.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — traffic annotation & session probe

Priya,

Appreciate the sample files — looks useful. Short answer: the fields that let us convert your workload into a GPU-footprint estimate are:

- Request type split (interactive chat vs batch) by percent at peak and averaged over the day.
- Prompt and response token histograms (not just averages): e.g., 0–32, 33–128, 129–512, 512+ bins.
- Concurrency by minute for a peak day (or synthetic hourly profile) and expected p95/p99 latency SLO.
- Percent of requests that use streaming vs non-streaming responses.
- Session reuse rate and average KV cache size per active session.
- Typical model family and preferred quantization/precision (if known).
- Any planned burst windows or campaign days (dates and expected multipliers).

I've attached a quick REDWOOD_SIZING_TEMPLATE that takes the above. If you can drop the CSV/JSON into that sheet (or paste histograms into the token tab) we can produce a first-cut fleet footprint and expected tail latency profile.

Proposed next steps:
1) You drop the populated template (or grant us access to the sample Drive folder)
2) We run a 48–72h sizing pass and share an initial fleet sketch and cost delta for dedicated tiers (reserved vs burst).
3) Quick follow-up call (30m) to walk assumptions and adjust for session affinity and KV cache sizing.

Would you be available Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT for the quick sync?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_sizing_template.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)]

From: Priya Shah <priya@horizonlabs.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Amit Desai <amit.desai@horizonlabs.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 07:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — traffic annotation & session probe

Sergio — thanks, that template looks perfect. Quick clarifications from our infra team (pasted from the sample logs):

- Peak split during surge: 78% interactive annotator calls, 22% lightweight API checks (heartbeat/metadata).
- Token histogram (interactive): 0–32: 12%; 33–128: 48%; 129–512: 32%; 512+: 8%.
- Streaming enabled for ~35% of interactive flows (real-time token display).
- Session reuse: average 1.9 requests/min per active session; active session median size ~640KB KV cache (mostly embeddings + metadata).
- Batch job profile: 1.2M requests/night with 75% of requests falling into 0–32 token bucket. Typical batch window: 01:00–05:00 PT.
- Latency target for interactive annotators: p95 < 220ms, p99 < 520ms (we tolerate occasional p99 spikes but would like guidance on expected tail under commit).

We attached the CSV and a small JSON sample in the Drive folder. Also noted the models we use: mix of open-weights LlamaX-13B quantized (8-bit) and a smaller in-house distilled 7B. Interested in your advice on whether to standardize on a single quantized profile for Dedicated.

We can do Thursday 10:00 PT — Marissa, will you join the sizing pass?

Thanks,
Priya

[Attachment: horizon_prompt_sample_populated.csv (csv, 54KB)]
[Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHorizonSamples]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@horizonlabs.ai>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — traffic annotation & session probe

Hi Priya — great data, thanks for the populated sample. Two quick notes from the sizing engine review (preliminary):

- With the token mix and session reuse you shared, our first-cut suggests a Dedicated reserved pool sized around 12 x A100-class slots (workload-weighted) to meet p95/p99 targets during the morning surge, with an overnight scaling group for batch throughput.
- Key caveat: KV cache memory per-session at ~640KB implies higher RAM pressure if session counts spike; we will include session-eviction heuristics in the runbook and test worst-case memory footprint during the 48–72h sizing pass.
- Recommendation: standardize on the 8-bit quantized LlamaX-13B for interactive flows (best latency/cost tradeoff) and route the distilled 7B for low-latency, extremely short prompts. We can model mixed routing in the sizing pass.

Next actions: I booked a 30m sync for Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT (calendar invite sent). Sergio / Karthik will run the sizing pass once we have Drive access (grant: marissa_cole@redwood.com).

If you want, I can include a short appendix in the deliverable that shows expected token-level cost deltas between reserved vs burst pricing and a sensitivity table for p99 variance.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwood.ai
